findings.text: argmax of the distance from the magnetic axis selects the X-point as the "lobe tip" -- the receipt's state_lobe_tip_rz equals state_rz to 1e-16 and image_lobe_tip_rz equals image_rz to 1e-16, so the reported lobe bearing 105.0 degrees is the axis-to-saddle bearing and lobe_tip_shift_mm equals the 0.3545 mm saddle displacement by construction; the fragment prints that coincidence as an independent lobe measurement at promoted-nodes-xpoint-angles.html:44, and the closing paragraph's "the direction that changes most is the lobe at +0.01 degrees" is the same displacement re-expressed.

the sentence "split by selection source they resolve as the table does rather than as the halves do" is contradicted by the table it introduces, whose interior-flood rows read 1.058e-09 Wb upper against 2.621e-02 Wb lower, so the half asymmetry survives inside a single selection source and the mechanism paragraph leaves that seven-order difference unexplained.

baseline_suite and after_suite are free prose rather than the required JSON (revision, command, exit_status, log_path, completed, failure_count, failure_ids), and the named pytest log artifacts-path-gate.log carries no revision or tree header, so the suite delta cannot be read from the record as filed.

the lane gate ran at f77fe72e4 and the delivered head is dc8e1a67a, contrary to the brief's "Gate. Run the lane gate at the final head, not at an earlier commit"; the measured sources are byte-identical across that gap so the numbers stand, but the gate log names no delivered revision.

the zoom locator is a 6 mm rectangle on a whole-machine panel, a few pixels at served width and drawn beneath the X-point markers, so the caption's claim that the left panel "carries the locator" shows a reader a blue speck rather than a locator.
